1.title: Documentation, Life-Cycle, Change and Configuration Management
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Documentation, Life-Cycle, Change and Configuration Management. It covers the exam area three point zero Network Operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. three point one Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures: documentation (physical versus logical diagrams, rack diagrams, cable maps, network diagrams at layers one, two and three, asset inventory, I P address management, S L A (service level agreement), wireless survey and heat map). Life-cycle management (E O L, E O S, software management, decommissioning). Change management. Configuration management (production, backup, baseline or golden configuration). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three point zero Network Operations (nineteen percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Documentation
1.text: Documentation. The figure shows this: Types of network documentation: diagrams, inventory, I P A M, S L A and heat maps.

1.title: Documentation, continued
1.text: Documentation. Physical diagram. Where equipment and cables physically are. Logical diagram. How data flows: I P addresses, V L A Ns, routing, zones. Rack diagram. Which device sits in which rack unit. Cable map or diagram. Where each cable runs and its labels. Network diagrams by layer. Layer one (cabling), layer two (switches, V L A Ns), layer three (subnets, routing). Asset inventory. Hardware, software, licensing and warranty support records.

1.title: Documentation, continued
1.text: Documentation. I P address management (I P A M). A tool that tracks subnets, addresses and D H C P or D N S usage. Service-level agreement. A contract defining expected service, uptime and response times. Wireless survey or heat map. Maps signal strength and coverage of the Wi-Fi. Exam tip: Physical diagram equals where things are. Logical diagram equals how traffic flows. A heat map shows wireless coverage gaps.

1.title: Life-cycle management
1.text: Life-cycle management. End-of-life (E O L). The vendor stops selling the product. End-of-support (E O S). The vendor stops patches and support; plan replacement before this date. Software management. Patches and bug fixes, O S updates, firmware updates, applied with testing and a rollback plan. Decommissioning. Safely retiring a device: remove from service, wipe data and configuration, update inventory and documentation, dispose responsibly.

1.title: Change management
1.text: Change management. A formal process that makes changes safe and traceable: request (service request tracking), assessment of risk and impact, approval, scheduling in a maintenance window, implementation with a rollback plan, testing, and documentation.

1.title: Configuration management
1.text: Configuration management. Production configuration. What the device is running now. Backup configuration. A saved copy used to restore a failed or replaced device. Baseline or golden configuration. The approved standard used to build and compare devices; drift from the baseline is investigated. Exam tip: E O L means no longer sold; E O S means no longer supported. Plan replacement before end-of-support. Exam tip: Golden configuration equals approved standard; backup configuration equals restore copy; production equals what runs now.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A technician needs to see which V L A Ns and subnets exist and how they connect. Which document helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A logical network diagram. Logical diagrams show addressing and traffic flow.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A vendor announces it will no longer provide security patches for a switch model after a date. What is this called? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: End-of-support. E O S means the vendor stops patches and support.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A new router is being built. Which configuration provides the approved standard to start from? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The golden (baseline) configuration. The baseline is the approved standard.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Wi-Fi users in one corner complain of weak signal. Which document best shows the problem? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A wireless heat map. Heat maps show coverage and signal strength.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which step comes first in a formal change management process? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A documented change request with risk assessment. Changes start with a request and impact assessment.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which tool tracks subnets and addresses to avoid conflicts? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: I P address management. I P A M manages address allocation.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does E O L mean? Answer: The vendor stops selling the product. Question two. What does E O S mean? Answer: The vendor stops providing patches and support. Question three. What is a rack diagram? Answer: A diagram of which device occupies which rack unit.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is a golden configuration? Answer: The approved baseline configuration used to build and compare devices. Question five. Name one decommissioning step. Answer: For example wipe the data and update the inventory. Question six. What does an S L A define? Answer: Expected service levels such as uptime and response times.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Documents: physical versus logical; rack, cable, layer one or two or three diagrams; inventory; I P A M; S L A. Life-cycle: E O L (not sold), E O S (no support); patches, firmware; decommissioning. Change: request, assess, approve, schedule, implement with rollback, test, document. Configurations: production, backup, golden baseline. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
